purpose: Information bottleneck analysis: quantify MI loss through softmax+sampling via DPI
notes: Mathematical derivation + numerical verification. No model training. Codex R1 flagged overclaim (storage vs MI bits) -- corrected in proofs/information_bottleneck.md

purpose: Copy smoke test: gate on whether dynamics converge to correct embeddings. Tests E1, E5(lam=1), AR baseline, encoder-only ablation.
data_ref: synthetic (random V=64 L=8 sequences, generated on-the-fly)
notes: All gates PASS. E1 fix (added 0.1*CE to train readout_proj) restored 100% accuracy. E5 viable: wrong-attractor 0.01%, margin 9.33, rho 0.98. Encoder-only CONCERN expected (copy is trivial for encoder). Total wall time: 2274s (937+995+234+108).

purpose: Sort task: dynamics necessity test. Can UESD sort (data-dependent permutation) where encoder-only cannot? Addresses encoder confound from Exp A/B.
data_ref: synthetic (random V=64 L=8 sequences, sorted ascending)
notes: 5 training runs (1 E1 + 2 E5 + 1 AR + 1 enc-only). ALL GATES PASS but encoder-only CONFOUND persists: 99.99% token acc on sort (L=8, V=64). Sorting at this scale is solvable by attention without dynamics. E5 lam=0.1 best by gate criteria (acc=0.9999, WA=0.04%, conv=96.7%, rho=0.968). E5 lam=1.0 achieves 100% convergence but higher WA (0.14%). E1 rho exceeds 1 (max=1.045). Wall time: 3943s (E1:934, E5x2:2541, AR:302, Enc:165). DYNAMICS NECESSITY NOT CONFIRMED — need harder tasks (addition, dedup).

purpose: Compositional tasks: dynamics necessity (hard). Tests addition (carry propagation, O(L) sequential depth) and dedup (non-bijective counting/grouping). Addresses encoder confound from Exp A/B/C.
data_ref: synthetic (V=64 L=8, addition interleaved pairs + dedup random with repeats)
notes: 10 training runs (2 tasks x 5 models each). DYNAMICS NECESSITY CONFIRMED ON ADDITION: encoder-only 73.16% token acc (0.11% seq acc) vs E5 100%/100%. E1 fails on addition (CE stuck at 2.08 = ln(64)/2). Phase transition at step ~4000 for both E5 lambdas. Dedup: encoder confound persists (99.23% token, 95.70% seq). E1 works on dedup (99.97% token). Wall time: 8959s (addition: E1=1330, E5x2=2237, AR=232, Enc=122; dedup: E1=1055, E5x2=2228, AR=347, Enc=229).

purpose: Reversal main test: can dynamics solve non-trivial transformations? E1 vs E5 lambda sweep {0, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0}, AR baseline, encoder-only ablation.
notes: ALL GATES PASS. 7 runs (1 E1 + 4 E5 + 1 AR + 1 enc-only). Wall time: 5287s. Key findings: (1) All lambdas achieve 100% acc with 0% wrong-attractor rate. (2) Lambda=0 (pure CE) works perfectly — SC loss spontaneously decreases without penalty. (3) Lambda=0.1 gives best rho (0.962) — non-monotonic relationship. (4) Encoder-only CONCERN: 100% on reversal too, dynamics not proven necessary on these tasks. D5 basin perturbation results INVALID (bug fixed post-run, not re-evaluated).

purpose: Codex Evidence Gate controls for dynamics necessity claim. Three controls: CE-matched dynamics ablation, depth-matched encoder-only (4L/8L), 5-seed sweep.
notes: 13 training runs. CE-dynamics (UESD+pure CE, no SC) achieves 100%/100% — dynamics sufficient, SC not required. Deep encoders (4L/8L) also learn addition, so dynamics not strictly necessary. E5 has 40% failure rate (2/5 seeds stuck at CE=2.08 wrong attractors). Known seeding bug: set_seed called after model creation, fixed in code. Key finding: SC term can trap dynamics in wrong attractors. CE-only training more robust than E5. Wall time: ~12127s.

purpose: Properly-seeded 5-seed sweep: CE-dynamics vs E5 vs Encoder-2L on addition. Fixes D2 seeding bug (set_seed before model creation).
notes: 15 training runs (3 tracks x 5 seeds). CE-dynamics 100% reliable (5/5). E5 bimodal: seed=512 stuck at CE=2.08 wrong attractor (0% seq acc). Enc-2L bimodal: seed=1024 fails (69.3% tok). Seeding fix confirmed — results reproducible. Wall time: ~14481s total (~890s CE-dyn, ~971s E5, ~110s Enc-2L per seed).

purpose: D7 non-normality analysis: sigma_max/rho ratio on CE-dynamics vs E5. Tests Theorem 4 finite-T stability bound.
notes: 4 training runs (2 tracks x 2 seeds). SC loss increases non-normality by 28-35% (E5 kappa 1.85-2.12 vs CE-dyn 1.45-1.57). E5 seed=42 had very late phase transition (step ~10.5K) and highest kappa (2.12, SEVERE). Theorem 4 bound wildly conservative: sigma_max^10 up to 2750x predicted amplification, actual basin stability 99.7-100%. All rho near 1.0. Wall time: ~3718s.

purpose: Depth-matched encoder sweep (4L/8L) for parameter-efficiency comparison against UESD CE-dynamics (694K params).
notes: 10 training runs (2 depths x 5 seeds). enc_4L: seed=1024 fails (seq=0.8557), others converge. enc_8L: 5/5 reliable. UESD CE-dynamics (694K, 5/5) matches enc_8L reliability at 43% of parameters (694K vs 1615K). enc_4L (822K, comparable params to UESD) has 80% success vs UESD 100%. Wall time: ~889s (4L) + ~1572s (8L) = ~2461s total.

purpose: Trajectory Lyapunov analysis: product-Jacobian along dynamics path explains why sigma_max > 1 yet basin stability > 99%
notes: 4 training runs (2 tracks x 2 seeds) + trajectory Jacobian analysis. Key finding: Theorem 4 bound conservative by up to 1027x. Jacobian rotation (singular vector alignment as low as 0.105) prevents exponential blowup. E5 MORE trajectory-stable than CE-dynamics despite worse per-step metrics. Cumulative product sigma_max can shrink (non-monotonic). Dynamics self-organize to edge of chaos (lambda_max in 0.045-0.199). Connects to non-normal operator theory from fluid dynamics.

purpose: Phase transition dynamics: how trajectory stability evolves during training. Two tracks (CE-dynamics, E5), 40 diagnostic snapshots each.
notes: Two distinct stability mechanisms: CE-dynamics uses Jacobian ROTATION (alignment drops to 0.068), E5 uses sigma COMPRESSION (alignment stays >0.77). E5 Lyapunov drops 80% vs CE-dynamics 45%. Three-phase regime (untrained/exploring/task-aligned) is CE-dynamics-specific. SC accelerates CE transition (step 2000 vs 3000). Conservatism paradox: E5 MORE stable but HIGHER conservatism (583x vs 106x).

purpose: D3b: Validate trajectory Lyapunov via autograd check, eps sweep, shuffled-trajectory ablation, corrected bounds
notes: Codex-mandated validation. Jacobian valid (autograd confirms). Lyapunov eps-robust. Alignment drops at eps=1e-5 (float32 floor). Shuffled test: temporal ordering reduces amplification by ~7% vs random permutation. Corrected conservatism: 718x (product-of-sigmas/actual), not 1027x. Rotation is Jacobian diversity at different trajectory states, not primarily learned temporal structure.

purpose: Multi-seed stability validation: 5 seeds x 2 tracks (E5, CE-dynamics) on addition. Tests whether two dynamical regimes are reproducible.
notes: 10 training runs. ALL SUCCESS. Two non-overlapping regimes: E5 highway (lyap 0.06, align 0.81, amp 1.8x, o/s>1.0) vs CE-dyn scattered (lyap 0.19, align 0.60, amp 6.8x, o/s<1.0). CE-dyn seed 1024 is an outlier (lyap=0.23, amp=9.9x). E5 CV 5% vs CE-dyn CV 12%. Self-consistency regularizes toward tighter attractor clusters. Wall time: 3.75 hours.

purpose: Reconsideration capacity: can UESD dynamics self-correct from wrong intermediate states?
notes: SC loss creates 30x energy wells (vs 1.1x for CE-dyn). E5 recovery monotonically increases with steps (pulled by energy gradient); CE-dyn peaks at +5 then declines. E5 better error correction (15.1% vs 8.7% at 1/4 corrupted) but both insufficient for full self-correction. Cross-example transplant had insufficient valid pairs. Corruption doesn't propagate to uncorrupted positions.

purpose: Causal carry probing: 3-phase investigation (probes, perturbation, surgery) of carry propagation in UESD dynamics
notes: CARRY INFO DECODABLE BUT NOT CAUSALLY RELEVANT. Surgery flips carry with 100% immediate success but zero output change at all steps/positions. dynamics_ce: parallel resolution at step 1, avg persistence 0.177. E5: one-step delay (carry_in at step 2 not 1), subtle wavefront in perturbation analysis, stronger self-healing (persistence 0.074). E5 carry_out degrades at late steps (SC loss compresses representation). Directional causal structure present (leftward propagation) but computation is parallel.

purpose: Error function comparison: E3 denoising vs E5 self-consistency vs CE-dynamics on identical architecture
notes: THREE DISTINCT DYNAMICAL REGIMES confirmed. E3 is a third regime: lowest lyap (0.063), lowest amp (1.89), highest overshoot (1.127), best denoiser (11% residual at sigma=0.5). E3 implicitly achieves self-consistency (SC=0.000365) without SC loss. Hybrid update pattern: starts like CE (6.04) but contracts like E5 (0.25). All three reach perfect accuracy -- error function shapes geometry, not performance.

purpose: Thinking emergence: do dynamics progressively resolve carry chains in a wavefront pattern?
notes: CE-dynamics computes in PARALLEL (all positions stabilize at step ~2, zero carry-chain correlation). E5 shows weak sequential pattern (LSB first, r=+0.13) but has 128x SC loss bug. Progressive computation confirmed (monotonic improvement, zero backtracking after step 4). CE-dynamics uses only 40% of dynamics budget (steps 1-4 of 10). E5 results unreliable due to SC loss bug.

purpose: Energy landscape cartography: basin structure, radius, PCA slicing, path efficiency for E5 and CE-dynamics
notes: E5 is genuine fixed-point attractor (energy drops 900x to 0.02). CE-dynamics is NOT fixed-point (energy plateaus at 19-31, only 2x reduction). CE has WIDER basins (100% at scale=0.5 vs E5 99%) and MORE DIRECT paths (ratio 1.08 vs 1.24). CE step sizes nearly constant (ballistic computation) vs E5 exponential decay (convergent). CE states travel 4-5x farther. Energy landscape flat for CE (2% variation) -- basins determined by dynamics, not energy wells.

purpose: Adaptive halting: PonderNet-style difficulty-dependent compute allocation test
notes: Carry-chain correlation VANISHES under halting pressure (spread 0.47->0.05->0.001). Model needs ~6 steps minimum even at beta=1.0. Supports T5 parallel computation thesis. ~23% examples halt by step 1 at beta=1.0 with 99.85% accuracy.

purpose: Dynamics transfer: do addition dynamics transfer to subtraction/comparison?
notes: WEAK TRANSFER. Random untrained dynamics achieve 99.51% on subtraction (trained dynamics only 0.42% better). Comparison trivially solved by all conditions (100%). Target tasks too easy for meaningful transfer measurement. Need harder tasks (multiplication, modular arithmetic) to properly test dynamics transfer.

purpose: Step ablation falsification: does T=1 match T=10? The existential test of iterative dynamics.
notes: DYNAMICS OVERWHELMINGLY ESSENTIAL. CE ratio=0.015, E5 ratio=0.000. CE converges faster (92% at T=3 vs E5 23%) but degrades at high T (78% at T=32 vs E5 96%). All carry positions converge in parallel. CE has finite compute window (T=5-15). E5 stable to T=20. Codex T=1 prediction wrong (predicted mid-90%, actual 1.5%). Script crashed on JSON write (relative path) -- data recovered from stdout log.

purpose: Wrong-attractor rate: basin stability under noise injection for CE-dynamics and E5
notes: CE has infinitely wide readout basins (WA@0=0 even at sigma=2.0) but diverges with extra steps (WA@20=15.5% at sigma=0.01). E5 has narrower basins (escape at sigma=1.0) but more temporally stable (WA@20=2% at low noise). Neither track recovers -- all recovery values negative. CE state norm 6x larger than E5. Confirms D11 basin width, D19 high-T degradation. Script crashed on JSON write -- data recovered from stdout log.

purpose: Information trajectory: MI(s_t, y*) via probes at each dynamics step
notes: MONOTONIC INFORMATION ACCUMULATION confirmed. Probes lead readout by 1-2 steps (info in hidden states before readout-accessible). CE faster than E5. Zero backtracking for CE. All chain lengths converge in parallel. Shuffled controls at chance.
